text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocks(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Shoots(x, y) ::: x shoots at y.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Michael ::: Michael.
Windy ::: Windy.
Peter ::: Peter.
Class(x) ::: x is in Michael's class.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
Taller(Michael, y) ::: Michael is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y and y is taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x (Shoots(x, y) ∧ ¬Jump(x) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: Michael can block any shooting from a person as long as the person does not jump when shooting.
¬Blocks(Windy, y) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.
Conclusion:
GreatShooter(Windy) ::: Windy is a great shooter.
